extracted.intended_audience: authors/researchers preparing and submitting articles to arXiv
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for preparing and submitting scholarly articles (preprints) to arXiv, including acceptable file formats, figure requirements, file-naming rules, versioning, and administrative metadata. Focused on ensuring submissions are processable, archival, and correctly announced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitters must be registered authors
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept submissions only from registered authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must register and use their account to submit; third-party submissions (e.g., by secretaries) are discouraged because they often cause problems. "Taking responsibility" means the submitting author should be the author themself.

rubrics_metrics.name: License or licensing certification required
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitters must grant arXiv.org a non-exclusive and irrevocable license to distribute or certify that the work is available under another license that conveys these rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At submission you must either assign the required non-exclusive irrevocable distribution license to arXiv or certify an alternative license that conveys equivalent distribution rights. This is a mandatory administrative condition of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted text formats (ordered preference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your submission must be in one of the following formats (listed in order of preference): (La)TeX, AMS(La)TeX, PDFLaTeX; DOCX (Word 2007); PDF; PostScript; HTML with JPEG/PNG/GIF images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ArXiv prefers TeX/LaTeX as it is portable and transparent. Users of older word processors should save as PDF and submit that. Note explicitly: arXiv will not accept dvi, PS, or PDF created from TeX/LaTeX source, and scanned documents are not accepted. Choose formats that maximize long-term portability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit DVI/PS/PDF generated from TeX/LaTeX or scanned documents
rubrics_metrics.description: ArXiv will not accept dvi, PS, or PDF created from TeX/LaTeX source. Scanned documents are explicitly not accepted, regardless of format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you use TeX/LaTeX, submit the source in the recommended way (e.g., use PDFLaTeX when appropriate). Scanned files prevent proper archival and processing and are rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted figure formats and figure inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures may be PostScript (PS/EPS), JPEG (photographic), GIF or PNG (non-photographic/bitmaps), or PDF figures (only with PDFLaTeX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the most appropriate format for the figure type (EPS for line drawings/plots; JPEG for photos; GIF/PNG for bitmaps). If figures are included in LaTeX source, use standard macro packages (e.g., graphics, graphicx) so figures render correctly. ArXiv cannot provide TeX help—seek help from colleagues for TeX-related issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure size and inclusion policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If figure files are too large they will hinder readers with poor network connections; reduce figure sizes where possible. ArXiv does not accept submissions with omitted figures even if you provide a link to another server.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of readers in low-bandwidth environments; include figures but optimize/compress them. See arXiv information on submission sizes and bitmapping help. If you have problems with a large submission, contact arXiv administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name character restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv will accept only these characters in file names: a-z A-Z 0-9 _ + - . , =. Any other character (e.g., spaces, question marks, asterisks) will cause the system to reject the file upload or submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only allowed characters to ensure portability and reduce archival risk. Filenames containing disallowed characters will cause upload/submission failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name case sensitivity and internal references
rubrics_metrics.description: File names and extensions are case sensitive on the arXiv system (e.g., Figure1.PDF and figure1.pdf are not the same).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that internal file references (for example, LaTeX \includegraphics commands) exactly match the case of the uploaded filenames regardless of whether your local system is case sensitive. Mismatched case will break figure inclusion or cause processing errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check metadata and processed files before final submit
rubrics_metrics.description: Before completing the final 'Submit Article' step, carefully check both the title/abstract metadata and the processed files for errors or formatting issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you see errors or are unhappy with formatting, correct them before final submit or contact arXiv administrators for problems you cannot resolve. Careful pre-submit checks reduce the need for corrections after announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsubmit option and pre-announcement edits
rubrics_metrics.description: If you discover an error after submission but before public announcement you may select the Unsubmit icon next to the submission on your user page to return it to incomplete status, allowing modification and later resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsubmitting removes the article from the processing queue; announcement will be scheduled based on the later resubmission time. Use unsubmit to correct issues prior to public announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edits before announcement do not create additional versions; replacement not new submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Edits before an article is publicly announced will not generate additional versions. The date stamp associated with the submission will be the time that the final 'Submit Article' step is completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make a new submission for a corrected article or for an erratum. Instead, replace the original submission. Replacing prior to announcement will not create an extra version but will affect the submission's timestamp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement timing and order (daily schedule and effect of edits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are normally announced on a daily schedule (no activity on weekends). Each day's submissions before 16:00 US Eastern are not made public until 20:00 US Eastern that same day (examples given). Submissions are listed in order based on the submission time (the last time the 'Submit' button was selected).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An edit and subsequent 'Submit' resets the submission time and thus changes position in the listings. Edits made between 16:00 and 20:00 will remove the submission from that day's announcements and delay it until the next day. Plan timing of final submit carefully if announcement timing or ordering matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide required administrative metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: The following information is required for submission: institutional affiliation for the author(s) and official report number(s) from the author(s)' institution(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you supply accurate affiliations and any institutional report numbers at submission time, as these fields are required for processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact arXiv administrators for unresolved problems
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have problems (for example with a large submission or processing issues), contact arXiv administrators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ArXiv staff can assist with administrative or system problems but cannot provide TeX help; seek local TeX help for formatting/source issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not create a new submission for corrections/errata
rubrics_metrics.description: DO NOT make a new submission for a corrected article or for an erratum. Rather replace the original submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the replace workflow to update the existing submission; this preserves the submission record and avoids duplicate entries.
